what_it_does: Modern video compression standards like VVC (Versatile Video Coding — the newest international standard for squeezing video into smaller files) require several different mathematical transforms that convert image data from the pixel domain into a frequency domain where redundancy is easier to remove. Two important transforms are DCT-2 and DST-7; in current hardware, each gets its own separate circuit, which wastes chip area. This paper observes that the mathematical relationship between DCT-2 and DST-7 — specifically a "transfer matrix" that converts one into the other — has a diagonal structure that can be exploited. By applying a least-squares optimization (a standard technique for finding the best approximate solution) to make that transfer matrix as sparse as possible (meaning most entries become zero and can be skipped), a single shared circuit of simple shift-and-add units can compute all the required transforms for multiple block sizes (4 through 32 pixels wide). The result is one piece of hardware doing the job that previously required several, saving silicon area without a meaningful loss in video quality.
